Diffusion on a graph, solved with modelcompR

Source: R/integrations.R
graph_diffusion.Rd

Solves the graph heat equation $$\frac{du}{dt} = -\kappa\, L\, u,\quad u(0) = u_0,$$ with \(L = D - A\) the Laplacian ("laplacian") or \(I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}\) ("normalized_laplacian"), where \(A_{ij}\) is the weight of the edge from \(j\) to \(i\) and \(D\) holds the weighted in degrees. For an undirected graph the solution conserves \(\sum_i u_i\) under the plain Laplacian and tends to the mean.

Usage

graph_diffusion(
  g,
  u0,
  times,
  rate = 1,
  operator = c("laplacian", "normalized_laplacian"),
  alg = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

g

A graph_data object.

u0

Initial value per node (numeric vector of length num_nodes).

times

Times at which to return the solution; the first is the start.

rate

Diffusion rate \(\kappa\).

operator

"laplacian" or "normalized_laplacian".

alg

A modelcompR algorithm; default modelcompR::Tsit5().

...

Passed to modelcompR's solve() (for example abstol).

Value

A matrix with one row per time and one column per node, with the times in attribute "times".

Details

The ODE is solved by modelcompR (ODEProblem() and solve() with Tsit5() by default); graphlearnR has no integrator of its own. This is an optional bridge: modelcompR must be installed, and the solve runs on R numerics, so no gradients flow back to torch. It is a mechanistic simulation tool, not a neural ODE layer.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("modelcompR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  g <- graph_data(edge_index = rbind(1:3, 2:4), num_nodes = 4, directed = FALSE)
  graph_diffusion(g, c(1, 0, 0, 0), times = c(0, 1, 5))
}
#>              1         2         3         4
#> [1,] 1.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> [2,] 0.5238153 0.3087569 0.1235759 0.0438519
#> [3,] 0.2728255 0.2594370 0.2405384 0.2271991
#> attr(,"times")
#> [1] 0 1 5
